2. The plaintiff-respondent Nos. 1 and 2 filed the aforesaid suit stating, infer alia, that the land of CS Khatian No. 122 comprising 34.64 acres of land belonged in equal share to Raj Chandra Mondal and Lechu Mondal, sons of late Kanai Mondal. Raj Chandra Mondal died leaving wife Rajrani Mondal and son Rai Charan Mondal. Rajrani Mondal sold her interest to Keru Mondal and Khetra Mondal and delivered possession to them. Keru Mondal died leaving 2 sons, Fatik Mondal and Natu Mondal and they inherited the property left by their father. Khetra Mondal died leaving 2 daughters by name Kazali Dasi and Bilashi Dasi. Kazali Dasi recorded the land she got in the name of her minor son Dowri Mondal in the RS record and Bilashi Dasi recorded her share of the property in the name of her minor son Sree Mohon in the RS record. On the death of Rajrani Mondal her son Rai Charan Mondal inherited her remaining interest. Rai Charan Mondal died leaving wife Maha Dasi who sold her inherited share measuring 2.82-1/2 acres of land to Narendra Sarker, son of Umesh Sarker. Lechu Mondal died leaving sons-Krishna Mondal and Joy Gopal Mondal. Krishna Mondal sold 1.98 acres of land out of his share to Abdur Rahman and Torap Ali Dewan and delivered possession to them. Torap Ali Dewan sold 0.33 acre of land to Mofazzal and his wife and they exchanged the same with the plaintiffs. Joy Gopal Mondal died leaving 2 sons, Kartik Mondal and Gonesh Mondal. Gonesh Mondal exchanged his share with his brother Kartik Mondal and thereby Kartik Mondal became 16 annas owner of the property left by Joy Gopal Mondal in Sarabo Mouza within Savar and Gonesh Mondal in exchange got in his share property in Kanakbari Mouza. Property of the successive heirs of Raj Chandra Mondal and Lechu Mondal and the property of the purchasers from the heirs of said two original owners was recorded in the SA record. It is the further case of the plaintiff-respondents that in 1950 Ananda Mohan Mondal, Gobinda Chandra Mondal, Gouranga Mondal and Fatik Chandra Mondal, sons of Durga Charan Mondal, the relations of the successive heirs of Raj Chandra Mondal and Lechu Mondal, fell in distress and took shelter in the house of Krishna Mondal and others and started living in a small portion of the land of CS Khatian No. 122 and, as such, their names were recorded in SA Khatian No. 185 along with the names of the successive heirs of the original owners. The said relations of Raj Chandra Mondal and Lechu Mondal later on left the house of Krishna Mondal and others. Rajrani Mondal transferred 2.82½ acres of land to Sachi Ram and Sachi Ram sold the said land to the plaintiffs and delivered possession. Krishna Mondal and others transferred 31.04 acres of land out of the land of suit khatian to the plaintiffs. As the plaintiffs purchased land of CS Khatian No. 122 from Kartik Mondal and as there was amicable partition amongst Kartik Mondal and Gonesh Mondal, sons of Joy Gopal Mondal and thereupon Kartik Mondal got land of Mouza Sarabo in his share and Gonesh Mondal got the land or Mouza Ganakbari so to avoid future complication Gonesh Mondal's son Haripada Mondal executed “নাদাবি পত্র” in respect of the land of Mouza Sarabo. The total quantity of land in CS and RS is 34.64 acres of land and out of that plaintiffs are claiming 32.63 acres of land although their kabalas reflect 35.12½  It is the specific case of the plaintiffs that they are in possession of the land in suit and the land recorded in SA Khatian No. 185 was correctly recorded in RS (DP) Khatian No. 170 in the name of the plaintiffs vendor Krishna Chandra Mondal and others but later on in the finally published RS Khatian No. 42 wrongly names of Ananda Mondal, Gobinda Mondal, Fatik Mondal, sons of Durga Charan Mondal, and Genesh Chandra Mondal son of Joy Gopal Mondal were recorded and their address has been shown in India and in the middle of 1992 plaintiffs came to know about the wrong preparation of finally published RS record and as because of the wrong entry in the record of rights serious injury to their right actually arising they are constrained to file the suit. 

 3. The suit was contested by the defendant No.1, herein the appellant and the defendant No.2, Deputy Custodian of Vested Property as well as by the defendant No.5 (Respondent No.6 herein) by filing separate sets of written statements. The case of the contesting defendant Nos. 1 and 2 was that plaintiffs had no causes of action for the suit and the suit has been filed to grab the land of the government raising claim on the basis of false and forged papers. The specific cases of the said defendants was that land of SA Khatian No. 185 has been listed as enemy property, as the real owners left for India and staying there and, as such, their property was listed as enemy property, that RS Khatian No. 42 has been prepared in the light of the SA Khatian No. 185 and the same has been prepared correctly, that the land in suit is being managed by the Government, that the plaintiffs have no possession in the land in suit. 

 5. On appeal the High Court Division reversed the finding of the trial Court as to limitation holding that against the wrong entry in the SA and RS Khatian suit was not needed be filed within 6 years from the date of knowledge thereof and also from the date of final publication of the said Khatians but from the date of invasion made on the basis of wrong record of rights. The High Court  Division further held that the date of cause of action in the suit is not the essence of the suit and, as such, filing of written statement denying the title and possession of the plaintiff in the land in suit can even be a cause of action of the suit and thus the suit cannot be held to be barred by limitation. The High Court Division was of the view that treating a portion of the land as recorded in SA Khatian later on in RS Khatian as vested property was not legal. The High Court Division further held that from the side of the defendant Nos. 1 and 2 no material whatsoever was placed as to how Ananda Mohan Mondal and others became co-sharers in the land as recorded in SA and RS Khatians and thereupon held that Ananda Mohan Mondal and others have got no interest in the land in the suit and, as such, the land in suit cannot be treated as vested property. 

 6. Leave has been granted to consider the submissions that the judgment of the High Court Division was not a proper judgment of  reversal and the High Court Division was wrong in holding that there was no presumption of correctness of RS Khatian under the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act and the observations in that behalf on the basis of which only the suit was decreed, were not at all correct and justified, that there having no consideration of the plaintiffs' case and the finding made by the trial Court against the plaintiffs, the decree passed in their favour is not legal and sustainable in law. 

 8. The land in suit as recorded in CS Khatian belonged to Raj Chandra Mondal and Lechu Mondal. Raj Chandra Mondal died leaving wife Rajrani Mondal and a son by name Rai Charan Mondal and Rai Charan Mondal died leaving wife Maha Dasi. Lechu Mondal died leaving 2 sons Krishna Mondal and Joy Gopal Mondal. Joy Gopal Mondal died leaving sons Kartik Mondal and Gonesh Mondal. The aforesaid genealogical tree of the CS record tenants was not challenged or proved as not correct by the contesting defendant Nos. 1 and 2. The fact of transfer by the successive heirs of Raj Chandra Mondal and Lechu Mondal deposed by PW 1, plaintiff No.1, was not challenged by the defendant Nos. 1 and 2, nor proved the statement made by PW 1 as incorrect. The fact of amicable partition between Kartik Mondal and Gonesh Mondal, sons of Joy Gopal Mondal and thereupon Kartik Mondal got the property in Sarabo Mouza has not been disproved by the contesting defendant Nos. 1 and 2, rather plaintiffs have proved the said fact by the “নাদাবি” deed (Exhibit 6) executed by the son of Gonesh Mondal. It may be mentioned part of the property out of 32.63 acres of land of Sarabo Mouza in Savar PS has been treated as vested property claiming to be the property of Ananda Mohan Mondal, Gobinda Chandra Mondal and Fatik Chandra Mondal, sons of Durga Charan Mondal and Gonesh Chandra Mondal, son of Joy Gopal Mondal. It has already been mentioned that by amicable partition between Kartik Mondal and Gonesh Mondal, sons of Joy Gopal Mondal, the property in Sarabo Mouza was obtained by Kartik Mondal and in exchange thereof Gonesh Mondal got the property of Kanakbari Mouza. It is the definite case of the plaintiffs that Ananda Mohan Mondal, Gobinda Chandra Mondal, Gouranga Mondal and Fatik Chandra Mondal, sons of Durga Charan Mondal having had fallen in distress in the year 1950 took shelter in the homestead of Krishna Mondal and others and later on they left the homestead of Krishna Mondal and others. It is also the case of the plaintiffs that sons of Durga Charan Mondal had no interest in the land owned by Raj Chandra Mondal and Lechu Mondal and later on inherited by their successive heirs. From the contesting defendants' (defendant Nos. 1 and 2) side no material has been placed on the record to show that sons of Durga Charan Mondal had acquired interest in any manner in the land recorded' in CS Khatian No. 122, later on in the SA Khatian No. 185 and RS Khatian No. 42. 

 9. Part ofthe property in suit has been treated as vested property on the basis of the SA Khatian No. 185 and the finally published RS Khatian No. 42. It is the case of the plaintiffs that SA Khatian No. 185 and RS record was wrongly prepared in the name of sons of Durga Charan Mondal and that also the name of Gonesh Chandra Mondal was wrongly entered in the RS Khatian No. 42 since by amicable partition Kartik Mondal, son of Joy Gopal Mondal got the property of Sarabo Mouza and in exchange thereof Gonesh Chandra Mondal, son of Joy Gopal Mondal got the property of Ganakbari Mouza. The plaintiff in support of the fact of amicable partition has put into evidence Exhibit 6, deed of 'nadabi' executed by Haripada Mondal, son of Gonesh Chandra Mondal. 

 11. The appellant has based its claim as regard the property in suit or part of the property in suit as of being the vested property on the RS Khatian and the census list of the vested property. It may be mentioned census list as it appears has been prepared either on the basis of SA or RS Khatian. In the RS Khatian along with the names of the heirs of the CS recorded tenants and their transferees names of the sons of Durga Charan Mondal have also been recorded and in the RS Khatian address of Durga Charan Mondal's sons and Joy Gopal Mondal's son Gonesh Chandra Mondal has been shown as India and consequent thereupon,. there is an entry in the RS Khatian to the effect "পক্ষে" Custodian land and building". 

 12. The learned Counsel for the appellant has submitted that as in the RS Khatian No. 42 prepared under section 144 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 (the Act) names of sons of Durga Charan Mondal as well as Joy Gopal Mondal's son Ganesh Chandra Mondal appear and consequent thereupon as there is presumption of correctness of the entries in the said RS Khatian under section 144A of the Act, as such, treating the property of the said persons as vested property was quite legal. The presumption as regards the entries in the RS Khatian so attached under section 144A of the Act is rebuttable by leading evidence from the side of the person questioning correctness of the entry made therein. It is in the evidence of PW 1 that Durga Charan Mondal's sons having had fallen in distress some time in 1950 came to the house of Raj Chandra Mondal and Durga Charan Mandai's sons had no title in the land of Raj Chandra Mondal and Lechu Mondal and they stayed for some time but later on left the house of Raj Chandra Mondal. It is also in the evidence of PW 1 that names of Durga Charan Mondal's sons were wrongly recorded in the SA and RS Khatian. As against the aforesaid contention of PW 1 the evidence of DW 1 is that Ananda Mohan Mondal and others sons of Durga Charan Mondal were the SA recorded tenants and that they left for India at the time of war of 1965 and thereupon their land has been listed as vested property. This witness in cross-examination has stated that he cannot say on what basis names of sons of Durga Charan Mondal have been recorded in SA Khatian and that he cannot say Durga Charan Mondal's sons and Joy Gopal Mondal's son Gonesh Chandra Mondal at what point of time went to India. Since from the materials on record it is seen that there was no. basis for recording names of Durga Charan Mondal's sons and also name of Gonesh Chandra Mondal in the SA Khatian and also for making entries in the RS Khatian as regards address of Durga Charan Mondal's sons and. Joy Gopal Mondal's son Gonesh Chandra Mondal shown as India has no basis, so the said entries in the RS Khatian were incorrect. Moreover, the Exhibit 6, Nadabi deed executed by Gonesh Chandra Mondal's son of Haripada Mondal reflects the fact of amicable partition of the property of Joy, Gopal Mondal between his, sons Kartik Mondal and Gonesh Chandra Mondal and thereupon Kartik Mondal got the property of Sarabo Mouza wherein the land in suit situates. It is seenfrom the materials on the, record that the entry in the RS Khatian as regards name of Gonesh Chandra Mondal, son of Joy Gopal Mondal reflecting interest in the land of Sarabo Mouza, wherein the land situates, is not correct. Since the presumption of correctness that has been attached to the RS Khatian by  the provision of section 144A of the Act has been rebutted and consequent thereupon recording of names of Durga Charan Mondal's sons and Joy Gopal Mondal's son Gonesh Chandra Mondal was not correct, rather there was no basis for entering their names in the RS Khatian No. 42 and, as such, defendants (defendant Nos. 1 and 2) case of vested property on the basis of wrong entry of the names of persons having no title and interest in the land so listed in the RS Khatian in question has no leg to stand, rather the property in suit has been listed in the census list as vested property without ascertaining the correct position or without ascertaining particulars of the persons who have, in fact, right, title and interest in the land in suit. It appears the vested property authority has prepared the census list merely on the basis of wrongly prepared RS Khatian No. 42, and without ascertaining the real state of the matter is the property in suit in reality belongs to whom. 

 13. The learned Counsel for the appellant has submitted that in the background of the gazette notification dated December 3, 1965 property that assumed character of enemy property, later on vested property, vested in the Government, as such, transfers made in 1970 by successive heirs of CS recorded tenants and the purchasers therefrom were not legal and valid and the Exhibit 6, Nadabi deed, executed by Gonesh Chandra Mondal's son Haripada Mondal ought notto have been taken into consideration for the purpose of arriving at a decision that Gonesh Chandra Mondal, son of Joy Gopal Mondal ceased to be the owner of the land of Sarabo Mouza because of amicable partition between the brothers, namely Kartick Mondal and Gonesh Chandra Mondal, sons of Joy Gopal Mondal. We have already observed that part of the land recorded in RS Khatian has been listed as vested property on the basis of entry in the said Khatian. Since incorrectness of the entries in the said RS Khatian No. 42 in so far names of Durga Charan Mondal's sons and the name of Gonesh Chandra Mondal, son of Joy Gopal Mondal have been established by the respondent Nos. 1 and 2, as such, treating the property in suit as vested property on the basis of said wrong entries was illegal. As to treating the property of Gonesh Chandra Mondal son of Joy Gopal Mondal in Sarabo Mouza as vested property is, also not correct, as firstly it is in the evidence of DW 1 that he cannot say when Gonesh Chandra Mondal left for India and second by the Exhibit 6 it has been established by the respondent Nos. 1 and 2 that Gonesh Chandra Mondal ceased to have any interest in the land of Sarabo Mouza because of amicable partition with his brother Kartik Mondal. So there being no reliable evidence that the property legally vested in the Government as enemy property, later on vested property, as such, because of the notification of December 3, 1965 it cannot be said property in suit has vested in the Government as enemy property, later on vested property. 

 14. It is seen from the judgment of the High Court Division that the said Division: was of the view that RS record was prepared in terms of the provisions as are in Chapter IV of Part IV of the Act and thereupon expressed the view that presumption of correctness as to the entries in the SA and RS record finally published under section 19(3) in Chapter IV has no presumption of correctness. As against the said finding of the High Court Division the learned Counsel for the appellant has submitted that R'S record has been prepared as per provision of section 144 of Chapter XVII of part V of the Act and to the entries in the RS record so prepared under the said section of the Act presumption of correctness has been attached under section 144A of the Act. We have already held that presumption so attached under section 144A of the Act to the Khatians prepared under section 144 of the Act is rebuttable and the respondent Nos. 1 and 2 has rebutted the correctness of the entry made therein as regard the name of Durga Charan Mondal's sons and name or Gonesh Chandra Mondal son of Joy Gopal Mondal and, as such, the finding of the High Court Division that presumption of correctness as regard the entries in the RS Khatian is not available, is not correct, as submitted by the learned Counsel for the appellant, though of merit but for that the decision arrived at by the High Court Division that the property in suit is not vested property has not been materially affected since it has been established by the respondent Nos. 1 and 2 that recording of the names of Durga Charan Mondal's sons as well as Gonesh Chandra Mondal, son of Joy Gopal Mondal in the SA and RS record of rights was not correct.
